subject: RE: Third-party infringement notice — response plan and MSA redlines
messages:
From: Vanessa Morris <vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Third-party infringement notice - Redwood exposure

Soojin,

Attached is a notice we received this morning from a third party alleging patent infringement related to a feature that runs on Redwood as part of our integration. Legal copied me and asked to flag any vendor obligations under our MSA/order form. The notice asks for indemnification and immediate remediation steps.

Can Redwood confirm whether (1) this claim falls within your indemnity obligations under our current MSA, and (2) whether Redwood will assume defense or provide a defense with reservation of rights?

We are preparing a preservation and mitigation plan; please see the attached Atlas_Infringement_Notice.pdf and let us know how quickly you can provide a redline or proposed language. Our timeline is tight — we need an initial response to the claimant within 72 hours.

Thanks,
Vanessa Morris
VP, Legal Operations
Atlas Cloud

Attachments: Atlas_Infringement_Notice.pdf (PDF, 145 KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Morris <vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2025 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Third-party infringement notice - Redwood exposure

Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the notice. I’ve looped in Rishi (legal) and Lauren (AE). Rishi: can you take the lead on the redlines and defense position? Lauren: FYI on account risk and timelines — Atlas is asking for an initial reply to the claimant in 72h.

High level from our side: we need to know whether the alleged claim implicates core Redwood model IP vs. customer-provided integration code. If it’s the latter, we’ll likely push for Atlas to handle defense or at least accept settlement control with Redwood approval. If the issue is with a Redwood-provided component we’ll evaluate coverage under the MSA but will want guardrails (caps, carve-outs for open-source, cooperation clauses).

I’m happy to coordinate a short sync between counsel if helpful. Also attaching a short checklist of the info Rishi will need to draft a response.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment: request_checklist.txt (list of claimant docs, timestamps, integration details)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Morris <vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Third-party infringement notice - Redwood exposure

Team / Vanessa —

Thanks — I reviewed the notice. Preliminary thoughts:

- Scope: The notice references a claim tied to a specific inference path that appears to be driven by customer-configured prompts and an integration wrapper. If Atlas confirms this is not a Redwood core model change, it likely sits closer to customer-made modifications.

- Defense vs. Indemnity: Our standard MSA currently provides vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims "to the extent arising from Vendor's deliverables as shipped." However, the Order Form includes a broad customer obligation for custom integrations which could muddy the waters. We should avoid conceding defense control without settlement consent and require (i) prompt notice, (ii) opportunity to cure, and (iii) limits on settlements that bind Redwood.

- Proposed redline highlights (draft to follow):
  * Redwood will indemnify and defend Atlas for third-party claims to the extent the claim relates to Redwood-delivered software or services, excluding (a) modifications or integrations made by Atlas or its customers, (b) open-source components used under their existing licenses, and (c) content provided by Atlas customers.
  * Defense control: Redwood will have the right to conduct the defense with Atlas's reasonable cooperation; Atlas may participate with counsel of its choice at its own expense. Redwood will not enter into a settlement that admits liability or imposes equitable relief without Atlas's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
  * Caps & Remedies: Liability for IP indemnity will exclude consequential damages and be subject to the Order Form monetary cap. We should preserve injunctive relief carve-outs where appropriate.

Questions for Atlas (to Vanessa):
1) Can you confirm whether Atlas (or a customer) made any code changes to the inference pipeline tied to the allegation?
2) Does Atlas expect Redwood to indemnify for any settlement amounts that include non-IP related claims (e.g., data privacy)?

I’m preparing a marked redline and a defense control matrix for internal review; aiming to get that over to Vanessa within 6–8 hours.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: (to be shared) redwood_proposed_redlines.docx, defense_control_matrix.xlsx

From: Vanessa Morris <vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2025 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Third-party infringement notice - Redwood exposure

Thanks, Rishi. Quick answers:

1) Atlas IT confirms no customer code changes in the last 90 days to the integration wrapper; we are still validating telemetry but current signal points to the vendor-supplied runtime.
2) Atlas expects vendor coverage for IP-related settlement amounts. Non-IP claims will be evaluated separately.

We are comfortable with Redwood leading defense if you require that, but Atlas will want prior review of any settlement that imposes operational constraints on our production (e.g., blocking features). We can agree to participation at our counsel's expense.

I’ll wait for your redline. Our counsel is available for an afternoon call if that helps.

Vanessa

--
Vanessa Morris
VP, Legal Operations | Atlas Cloud
vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com

Attachment: Atlas_IT_validation_log.csv (internal log snippet)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Morris <vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Third-party infringement notice - response plan and commercial impact

Vanessa / team —

Quick commercial note to accompany Rishi's redline: Atlas is a strategic expansion account. If a prolonged injunction or production block is sought, the commercial fallout is material (revenue and customer churn). From the GTM side we can offer temporary mitigation options (feature flags, routing to a fallback model) while legal sorts the defense, but we cannot accept open-ended liability that would threaten our broader business.

Proposed commercial compromise for the Order Form:
- Redwood accepts indemnity and defense for third-party IP claims that arise from Redwood-delivered components used in the Atlas integration;
- Exclusions: modifications by Atlas/customers, OSS components, and customer-provided content;
- Redwood will retain defense control but will include Atlas in settlement decisions and will not agree to injunctive terms that would materially disrupt Atlas production without mutual agreement;
- If Atlas requires a higher indemnity cap for this deal, we can consider a limited uplift tied to a revenue-based surcharge — need to know if that is on the table.

Soojin: happy to join the call if you want to discuss tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: commercial_compromise_summary.pdf (one-pager)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Morris <vanessa.morris@atlascloud.com>, Atlas Cloud Legal <legal@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 May 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Redwood proposed redlines and next steps

Vanessa / Atlas counsel —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are Redwood's proposed redlines (redwood_proposed_redlines.docx) and a defense control matrix that maps responsibilities and timelines (defense_control_matrix.xlsx). Summary of Redwood's position:

- Redwood will indemnify and defend Atlas for third-party IP claims to the extent the claim relates to Redwood-delivered software or services used as shipped.
- Exclusions: modifications by Atlas or its customers; open-source components used pursuant to their licenses; customer-provided content.
- Redwood requests (i) prompt written notice, (ii) a 30-day cure opportunity where technically feasible, and (iii) Redwood control of exclusive defense with Atlas permitted to participate at its own counsel expense. Redwood will not agree to settlements that admit liability or impose injunctive relief affecting other customers without Atlas's prior written consent.
- Liability will be subject to the Order Form cap; Redwood will exclude consequential damages. If Atlas needs a higher cap, we can discuss a limited commercial uplift.

Next steps requested:
1) Atlas to confirm whether the claim is tied to a Redwood-delivered component or customer code (Atlas already indicated vendor signal; please confirm in writing).
2) Atlas legal to review the attached redlines and provide comments by EOD Monday so we can meet the claimant reply timeline.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-minute call Monday morning with Atlas counsel, Rishi, and Soojin.

We appreciate the urgency and will prioritize this internally.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142
